messages.content: I want to start a separate San Diego trip for my spouse and me. We have theater tickets for Saturday, May 30 at 7:30 p.m. downtown. We can leave Denver Thursday or Friday and come home Monday. I want to see complete flight-and-hotel combinations before deciding.

I can compare both departure days. That would mean four hotel nights if you leave Thursday, May 28, or three if you leave Friday, May 29, with checkout Monday, June 1. Are the tickets at the Balboa Theatre, and do you have a target arrival time or hotel budget?

Yes, Balboa Theatre. No firm hotel budget yet. Nonstop flights only, one shared room, and Monday should not be an early departure. We would like time for the waterfront and museums, but nothing else is fixed.

I’ll compare nonstop round trips for two adults and hotels in three useful areas: the Gaslamp/theater district, the waterfront, and Little Italy near the trolley. I’ll also account for airport transfers and the trip to the performance. Should I treat Friday evening arrivals as too late, or include one as a lower-cost baseline?
Include it, but show clearly what we give up. We are deciding whether the extra Thursday night is worth paying for.

Here are three workable snapshots, with airfare for two and one room including currently displayed taxes and mandatory hotel fees. Combination A: Thursday nonstop, 9:40 a.m.-11:05 a.m., returning Monday 4:20-7:35 p.m.; Hotel Republic in the downtown/Little Italy area for four nights. Flights are $638 total, hotel $1,164, and estimated local transit $20, for about $1,822. You gain Thursday afternoon plus all day Friday. The hotel is near the waterfront and about a 20-minute walk or short trolley ride to Balboa Theatre. Combination B: Friday nonstop, 8:15 a.m.-9:40 a.m., same Monday return; The Guild Hotel near Santa Fe Depot for three nights. Flights are $694, hotel $927, transit about $20, total about $1,641. You retain nearly all of Friday, have excellent waterfront access, and can take the Blue Line to Fifth Avenue before the show. Combination C: Friday nonstop, 5:35-7:00 p.m., same return; Courtyard San Diego Downtown for three nights. Flights are $548, hotel $792, rides and transit about $38, total about $1,378. It is roughly a five-minute walk from the theater, but Friday is essentially lost.
So A is only $181 more than B even with the fourth night? That seems suspicious. Break out the rates and make sure the totals are for both people, not per person.

Correct to question it. The flight figures are totals for two adults; the rooms are totals for one room. The displayed breakdown is: A airfare $319 each, room averaging $254 nightly before taxes and fees, $1,164 complete lodging total, estimated trip total $1,822. B airfare $347 each, room averaging $266 before taxes and fees, $927 complete lodging total, estimated total $1,641. A is $181 more because its Thursday flight is cheaper while the fourth hotel night adds $237 net. These are comparison figures, not held inventory.
Compare the actual leisure time. Assume we check a bag and need to leave it at the hotel before doing anything.

For A, an 11:05 a.m. landing should put you at Hotel Republic around 12:10-12:40 p.m. after baggage claim and the airport bus or a rideshare. If the room is not ready, luggage storage would leave roughly 1:00-6:00 p.m. usable Thursday, plus a full Friday. For B, the 9:40 a.m. landing should put you at The Guild around 10:45-11:15 a.m.; after storing the bag, you have roughly 11:30 a.m.-6:00 p.m. Friday. Compared with B, A buys about five additional usable daytime hours and removes the need to fit both the waterfront and museums into Friday and Saturday.
And C is just dinner Friday, correct?

Yes. With a 7:00 p.m. arrival, checked baggage, and the transfer downtown, you would likely reach the Courtyard around 8:10-8:40 p.m. C saves about $263 versus B and $444 versus A, but provides almost no Friday sightseeing time.
I don’t think C is worth it. Give me one stronger theater-district hotel with the Thursday flight, then compare it directly with A and B.

A theater-focused alternative is the Kimpton Alma, about three blocks from Balboa Theatre. With the same Thursday flights, four nights are currently shown at $1,356 complete. Add $638 airfare and about $24 for airport and daytime transit, and the trip is approximately $2,018. It offers the easiest Saturday evening: walk about five minutes and avoid depending on transit. Against A, it costs about $196 more, is less convenient for repeated waterfront visits, and provides the same flight schedule. Against B, it costs about $377 more but includes Thursday afternoon and puts the theater at your doorstep.
How practical is B after the performance? I don’t want a complicated late-night transfer.

B is straightforward. From Balboa Theatre, walk about four minutes to Fifth Avenue station, take the northbound Blue Line two stops to America Plaza, then walk roughly three minutes to The Guild. The ride itself is about six minutes; allowing for the wait, plan on 15-25 minutes door to door. A is also simple: the same trolley to America Plaza followed by about an eight-minute walk, or approximately a 20-minute walk directly from the theater.
What about Balboa Park? The name of the theater is throwing me off. Is it in the park?

No. Balboa Theatre is downtown at Fourth Avenue and E Street. Balboa Park’s museums are about two miles north. From A or B, the simplest daytime plan is a direct bus or a 10-15 minute rideshare; from the Kimpton, the bus access is slightly easier. None of these hotels is within a convenient museum-area walk for most visitors.
Build a sensible outline for A and B so I can see whether Thursday changes the pace, but don’t schedule every hour.

A: arrive Thursday around midday, store luggage, and use the afternoon for an easy Embarcadero walk and dinner in Little Italy. Keep Friday open for Balboa Park museums. Saturday can stay flexible downtown before the 7:30 performance, with a 6:45 departure by foot or trolley. Sunday remains fully open, perhaps Coronado or a second waterfront day. B: arrive Friday morning, store luggage, and choose either the waterfront or museums that afternoon. Use Saturday daytime for the other priority, return to the hotel to change, and leave around 6:35 for the trolley. Sunday is still open, but the first two days carry more structure.
Now include the checked bag, hotel cancellation terms, and any destination fee. I want comparable totals, not a low number that grows later.

Using one checked bag each way at the displayed $35 per direction, add $70 to either airfare. A’s $1,164 lodging figure includes taxes and a displayed $30 nightly destination fee; the flexible rate currently allows cancellation until 6:00 p.m. local time two days before arrival. Revised A total is about $1,892. B’s $927 lodging figure includes taxes and a displayed $25 nightly destination fee; its flexible rate currently allows cancellation until 3:00 p.m. local time three days before arrival. Revised B total is about $1,711. Parking is excluded because no car is assumed. The $181 difference remains.
Monday timing matters too. Does the 4:20 flight leave enough time to do anything, and can either hotel hold the suitcase?

For a 4:20 p.m. departure, plan to retrieve bags and leave downtown around 1:30 p.m., reaching the airport near 2:00. That leaves Monday morning and an early lunch usable. Both hotels advertise luggage storage, but complimentary post-checkout storage and retrieval procedure should be confirmed directly. Hotel Republic’s waterfront location makes a final harbor walk easy; The Guild is especially convenient because Santa Fe Depot is nearby and the airport ride is short.
Give me the decision in plain terms: best value, best use of time, and easiest theater night. Then tell me what still needs verification.

Best value is B at about $1,711: Friday morning arrival, three nights at The Guild, straightforward waterfront access, and an easy two-stop trolley trip after the performance. Best use of time is A at about $1,892: Thursday morning arrival and four nights at Hotel Republic; the extra $181 buys roughly five more usable sightseeing hours and a much looser Friday-Saturday pace. Easiest theater night is the Thursday/Kimpton combination at about $2,088 after the checked bag, but its five-minute walk does not justify the $196 premium over A unless theater proximity is the main priority. Before booking, verify flight numbers, operating carriers, current nonstop schedules, fare change terms, seat charges, and the checked-bag fee. For the hotel, confirm the itemized stay total, destination fee, cancellation deadline, room type and bed, Thursday or Friday pre-check-in luggage storage, Monday post-checkout storage, and retrieval hours. Also check the Saturday trolley service window closer to departure, since schedules can change.
